claim.summary: If δ is positive, c is nonnegative, c is strictly larger than B/(2δ), every residual is bounded by B, and every competitor has real-part gap at least δ, then every listed competitor has strictly smaller shifted squared modulus after the shift.
claim.gap_bound_condition: forall p in competitors, δ <= a - p.1
claim.conclusion: forall p in competitors, shiftedSqMod c p.1 p.2 < shiftedSqMod c a b

proves: explicit scalar lower bound c > B/(2δ) implies shifted dominance under residual and gap assumptions
does_not_prove: actual spectrum extraction from a matrix
construction of B from a matrix spectrum
construction of δ from a matrix spectral gap
strict spectral-abscissa hypothesis for a matrix eigenvalue
that a strict-abscissa eigenvalue of a real matrix is real
